policy_name: FINMA Guidance 08/2024: Governance and risk management when using artificial intelligence (FINMA-Aufsichtsmitteilung 08/2024)
covered_entities: FINMA-supervised institutions (banks, insurers, financial institutions, etc.)
covered_systems: AI applications developed or procured by supervised institutions, including outsourced/third-party AI
conditions: Expectations apply proportionately according to the materiality and risk of AI applications
objective: Communicates FINMA's observations from supervision and its expectations for how supervised institutions should identify, assess, manage and monitor risks arising from the use of AI, under existing technology-neutral governance and risk-management requirements.

related_policies.policy: FINMA Circular 2023/1 'Operational risks and resilience – banks'

conflict_rule: Guidance does not create new law; it explains how existing binding financial market law and FINMA circulars on governance and risk management apply to AI.

record_provenance.notes: finma.ch was blocked by the compilation environment's network policy; all clauses are paraphrases (text_is_verbatim=false) based on knowledge of the guidance and secondary summaries. Publication date 18 Dec 2024 confirmed by several sources (one secondary source says 8 Dec, likely an error). binding=false: FINMA guidance (Aufsichtsmitteilung) is not a legally binding act; it states supervisory expectations derived from binding law, so non-observance may have supervisory consequences. Status 'enforceable' denotes it is in force as current supervisory practice. official_languages assumed DE/FR/EN per FINMA's usual practice (German likely original); not verified. No amendment or successor found as of Nov 2026 (not exhaustively verified); FINMA indicated it will refine its expectations. Relationship to FINMA Circular 2023/1 is general (operational risk) and not confirmed as cited in the guidance.

clauses.original_text: Supervised institutions should define clear roles, responsibilities and competences for the development, implementation, use and monitoring of AI, with sufficient expertise; responsibility for decisions cannot be delegated to AI or to third parties, including where AI is outsourced.
clauses.requirement: assign clear responsibilities and competences for AI risks, also for outsourced/third-party AI, without delegating accountability
clauses.affected_asset: institution's operational, legal and reputational risk position; clients
clauses.applicable_systems: AI applications used by FINMA-supervised institutions
clauses.interpretation_notes: Paraphrase in English: the official FINMA PDF (DE original; EN version) could not be fetched (finma.ch blocked), so wording is reconstructed from knowledge of the guidance and search-result summaries; section headings are descriptive, not verified numbering. Guidance describes FINMA's supervisory expectations based on existing technology-neutral requirements, hence modality SHOULD.

clauses.original_text: Institutions should maintain an inventory of their AI applications and classify them by risk (materiality and specific AI risks) so that risk management measures can be applied proportionately.
clauses.requirement: keep a complete AI inventory with risk-based classification
clauses.purpose: proportionate, risk-based oversight of AI use
clauses.affected_asset: institution's operational, legal and reputational risk position; clients
clauses.applicable_systems: AI applications used by FINMA-supervised institutions

clauses.original_text: Institutions should set requirements in internal rules to ensure the completeness, correctness and integrity of data used for AI, and ensure the availability of and access to data.
clauses.object: quality of data used for AI applications
clauses.requirement: define and enforce data-quality requirements for AI data
clauses.purpose: prevent erroneous or biased AI results

clauses.original_text: Institutions should test AI applications before use and monitor them on an ongoing basis for performance, accuracy, robustness and stability, including data drift, with defined indicators and thresholds.
clauses.requirement: conduct pre-deployment testing and continuous monitoring of AI performance and stability
clauses.purpose: ensure AI remains accurate, robust and reliable

clauses.original_text: Results of AI applications should be explainable to the extent needed, so that the institution understands the drivers of results and can justify decisions to investors, clients, employees, the supervisor and the audit firm.
clauses.object: AI results and the decisions based on them
clauses.recipient: clients, investors, employees, FINMA, audit firm
clauses.requirement: be able to understand and explain AI-supported results and decisions
clauses.purpose: transparency and accountability toward stakeholders and supervisor

clauses.original_text: For material AI applications, institutions should provide for an independent review by qualified personnel (internal or external) not involved in the development of the application.
clauses.requirement: have material AI applications independently reviewed by qualified staff or third parties
